question.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{2}^{-2}\frac{1}{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-3$ and ${\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=10.$  What is the value of ${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
question.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{-2}\frac{1}{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ \frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ -\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ {\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =12+10 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$
